Hey Product Hunt, Praney here. I build Vois solo from Melbourne.  
  
Since the first Vois launch here, one complaint kept coming back from  
podcasters and narrators, and I had it myself: cloud voice tools charge per  
character, so every retake of the same paragraph costs money again. I  
started calling it the preview tax. You stop iterating, and the read stays  
mediocre.  
  
Vois 2.x is my answer: an ElevenLabs alternative that runs on your own  
machine. Every subscription has unlimited generation: no tokens, no usage  
meter. Retake a paragraph fifty times and your bill does not move.  
  
What is in 2.x:  
  
- Four engines, picked per job: Fast for drafts (about 3x real time on CPU,  
about 6x with GPU acceleration on Apple Silicon), Expressive for [...] This is the 2nd launch from Vois. View more

## Vois 2.0

Launching today

The ElevenLabs alternative with unlimited generation

An ElevenLabs alternative on your desktop. Subscriptions get unlimited text to speech: no tokens, no usage meter, no per-character fees. 100+ voices, voice cloning with consent built in, a multi-speaker timeline, mastering, export, and a CLI your AI agents can drive. 23 languages, 600+ with Omni on Pro. Used for audiobooks, podcasts, faceless YouTube videos, game NPC voices, tutorials, and courses, by makers at companies you would recognize. Launch: $10/mo for the life of your subscription.

Review ElevenLabs?

Reviewers mostly see ElevenLabs as one of the strongest voice AI tools for natural, expressive speech, with praise for realistic voiceovers, a large voice library, multilingual use, and straightforward API integration. Users often say it sounds more human than Polly, Google, or PlayHT, especially for narration, podcasts, and videos. Founders of Close and Typeahead also cite fast setup and strong results. The main complaints are inconsistent long-form output, weak handling of numbers, abbreviations, and some languages or accents, plus occasional pricing and support frustration.

## Similar Products [...] Naumaan Zahid

#### What's great

The voice quality is genuinely hard to tell apart from a real person. I've tried a few TTS tools and nothing comes close to how natural ElevenLabs sounds, especially with longer passages. The API is clean and well documented, which made integrating it into our workflow pretty painless. Voice cloning with just a short sample is wild.

#### What needs improvement

Pricing tiers could be more flexible for smaller teams who need decent volume but don't need enterprise features. Voice output can sometimes stumble on numbers and abbreviations, which means you have to spell things out manually. Would also love better accent control, right now you're mostly working with what the base voice gives you.

#### vs Alternatives

PlayHT [...] #### vs Alternatives

I also explored alternatives like Amazon Polly, Google Cloud Text-to-Speech, and PlayHT. While those platforms are solid for basic TTS use cases, ElevenLabs stood out because the voices felt significantly more natural and expressive, especially for storytelling, narration, and AI agent interactions. The balance between voice quality, ease of use, and API flexibility made it the better choice for my experiments.
